transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. Um... well, I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I'm here because... well, for a few months now, I've been noticing this sort of pattern, and it's been quite stressful. I supervise an administrative team, so I'm very used to keeping things organized and professional, but... well, my sister's medical appointments keep getting moved around without anyone telling me, and the bills keep showing up wrong. And people just suddenly seem to forget to call me back. 

Everyone keeps telling me they're just normal clerical mistakes, and I really don't want to come across as difficult or unreasonable to you, but... I just know they are keeping information from me on purpose. It really feels like they are trying to push me out of making any decisions regarding my sister's care. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me more about how you know that people are intentionally keeping information from you and trying to push you out of making decisions for your sister?

Well... I know it probably sounds a bit much when I say it out loud, and I really don't want to seem like one of those difficult, demanding family members. I try so hard to be understanding. But... well, in my line of work, you just learn to spot the difference between a simple oversight and an actual pattern. 

It's just that it happens every single time. Her appointments will get shifted to times I can't be there, and the bills are suddenly routed differently so I can't review them. And when I try to follow up to get it sorted out, the staff always say they just 'forgot' to return my call. 

Once or twice is a mistake, of course, and I'd be the first to forgive that. But this has been going on for months. Even though they smile and apologize and tell me it's just administrative errors... I can just tell. It’s too coordinated. They are definitely trying to quietly cut me out of the loop so I can't have a say in what happens with her. 

Does... does that make sense? I really hope I don't sound foolish or paranoid for thinking that. I just want to be a good advocate for her.
Have you noticed any other situations, outside of your sister’s medical care, where you feel people are deliberately keeping information from you or acting against you in a coordinated way?

Oh, no. No, not at all. Um... I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I think everyone is out to get me. I promise I'm not like that. 

At work, my team and I get along wonderfully. We communicate very well, and I trust my staff completely. And with my friends and the rest of my family, everything is perfectly fine, really. 

It's just... well, it's just this one specific situation with the medical staff and my sister's care. That's why it stands out so much to me, I think, because it's so different from how things normally operate in the rest of my life. I wouldn't even bring it up if it didn't feel so unusual and specific to them. 

Does that help clarify things? I just want to make sure I'm not painting the wrong picture of myself here, or sounding completely unreasonable to you.
Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something strongly that others didn’t seem to understand or agree with, even when there was no clear evidence to support it?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I really hope I'm not coming across as someone who just... imagines things or jumps to wild conclusions. I would hate for you to think that about me. 

In my job, I have to be very organized and rely on facts, so I always look for clear evidence before I make up my mind about something. So, no, I've never really had any sort of... unusual beliefs or anything like that where people didn't believe me. I'm usually a very grounded person, I promise. 

This situation with my sister's care is just... well, it's the only time I've ever felt so strongly about something that others are brushing off, but only because the pattern is just so obvious to me. But outside of that, no, absolutely not. 

I hope that makes sense? I just really want to assure you that I'm a very rational person, and I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.

Have you ever had a belief that something was happening or being done against you — even if others didn’t see it the same way — that turned out to be based on a misunderstanding or something that wasn’t actually happening?

Oh... um, no. I don't believe so. I mean... I always try to be very careful about not jumping to conclusions. I know how easy it is to misunderstand things, especially in an office setting where wires get crossed all the time. 

So if I ever feel like something is off, I always double-check myself first. I'll ask questions or look at the emails just to make sure I'm not... well, making a mountain out of a molehill. I really pride myself on being level-headed and fair to people. 

So, no, I can't think of a time where I was convinced of something like that and it turned out to be nothing. I always try to give people the benefit of the doubt until the facts just... well, until they speak for themselves, like with my sister's doctors. 

Does that... I mean, is that the kind of thing you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you ever had a strong belief about something that wasn’t true, even if you were absolutely sure it was at the time?

Oh... no, I haven't. Um... I know you've asked a few questions sort of like this, and I really hope I'm not frustrating you by giving the same answer. I just... I really want to be honest with you. 

I've always been someone who is very careful with the truth. If I'm not sure about something, I just say I don't know. I would never want to be one of those people who insists they are right when they are actually wrong. That's just... well, it's not who I am at all. 

I know it might sound strange that I'm so certain about what's happening at the hospital with my sister, but I promise I wouldn't say it if I hadn't thought it through completely. I really hope you believe me. I'm trying my best to give you good answers... am I doing okay?
Have you ever believed that you were receiving special messages or had a unique ability to understand things that others couldn't?

Oh, my... no. Um, definitely not. Special messages? Like... like on the television or something? No, I've never experienced anything like that. 

I hope these questions don't mean you think I'm... well, you know, losing my grip on things? I really am just a very standard, by-the-book kind of person. In my line of work, if it's not in a memo or an email, it doesn't exist, so I certainly don't look for hidden meanings or special signs. 

And as for a unique ability... no, not at all. I mean, I'm observant, and I pay close attention to details—which you kind of have to do when you're managing an office—but it's just from years of practical experience, not any sort of... special power or anything. 

I'm just a regular person, I promise. Is... is it normal for you to ask everyone these kinds of things? I just want to make sure I'm still being helpful and giving you what you need.
Have you ever had a belief that someone was acting against you or conspiring in some way, even if it was subtle or not obvious to others, outside of this situation with your sister's medical care?

Oh... um, no. No, I haven't. I mean, outside of what's happening with my sister... no, I've never felt like anyone was conspiring against me. 

I really try to get along with everyone. In my office, you know, as a supervisor, it's so important to build a good team environment, and you can't do that if you're always suspicious of people. If someone makes a mistake or if there's a disagreement, I just assume it's a normal workplace issue, not... not a plot or anything like that. I really value harmony and keeping things pleasant.

I know I must sound like a broken record, saying no to all these questions. I'm sorry if I'm not giving you the kind of answers you're looking for. I just... I really want to make sure you know that outside of this terrible situation with the hospital, my life is very normal and quiet. I hope that's okay? I'm really trying to be as helpful as I can.
Have you ever had a belief that turned out not to be true, but at the time, it seemed so real and logical to you that you were completely convinced it was true?

Oh... um, no. No, I really can't think of anything like that. I mean... I know we all make little mistakes sometimes, like thinking we left our keys on the counter when they were really in our purse, but... nothing big. Nothing where I was completely convinced of something that just wasn't true at all. 

I really pride myself on being very level-headed. I think you have to be, you know, when you're managing an office and keeping everything organized for everyone else. You have to stay grounded in the facts. I'd hate for anyone to think I was the sort of person who just... makes things up or gets carried away with silly ideas. 

I hope it's not frustrating that I keep saying no to these. I really am trying to think carefully before I answer. I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture of who I am. Am I... am I doing this right? I just want to be as helpful as possible.

Have you ever had a belief that you were being targeted, mistreated, or conspired against in any situation — even small or subtle — that others did not share or understand, even if you had no clear proof at the time?

Well... um. I wouldn't use a strong word like "conspired against," because that sounds so... dramatic, doesn't it? I really don't want to come across as one of those difficult, demanding people who just complains about everything. I always try to be polite to the staff. 

But... well, since you're asking, and I do want to be completely open with you... there is the situation with my sister's care that I mentioned earlier. That's actually why I'm here. 

For months now, I've just been seeing this very specific pattern. Her appointments keep getting moved around without me being told, and the medical bills keep showing up with all these little errors, and the staff somehow always "forget" to call me back. When I point it out, everyone just says, "Oh, it's just administrative mistakes, hospitals are so busy." But... well, I run an office. I know how scheduling and billing work. You don't just make that many mistakes with one specific patient. 

Even though everyone tells me it's nothing, I know they are purposely keeping information from me. I can tell they're trying to push me out of making decisions for her. I just... I know it's happening, even if other people don't see it. 

Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound unreasonable saying all that out loud. I really am just trying to look out for my sister, you know? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you can understand where I'm coming from. Is it okay that I feel that way?
Have you ever had any beliefs that weren’t shared by others, that felt completely real to you at the time, even if they turned out not to be true?

Oh... um, no. No, I really haven't. I know we sort of just talked about this, and I feel terrible just repeating myself... I hope you don't think I'm being difficult or holding anything back. 

I just... I've never had anything like that. Outside of this awful situation with the hospital, my life is just very ordinary. I go to work, I manage the office, I try to be a good sister... I don't have any strange ideas or beliefs that aren't true. I really pride myself on being very practical and grounded. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was the kind of person who just imagines things. 

I'm sorry, I know you have to ask these questions to do your job properly, and I want to be a good patient for you. I just... I don't have anything else to tell you on that front. I hope that's alright? I really am trying my best to give you what you need.
